sections.html:
Sherman sellers can go three ways: an agent, a do-it-yourself sale or an investor's cash bid. Let the state of the house and your deadline make the call. Sherman is the Grayson County seat on U.S. Highway 75, about seventy-five miles north of Dallas, so the buyer pool mixes commuters, local workers and investors. U.S. Highway 82 and State highways 11 and 56 also cross the city, which is worth a line in a listing aimed at commuters.

  • Agent: widest exposure, but you endure repair requests and wait on a buyer's loan.
  • On your own: contract and buyer questions are yours, and a title company handles the closing.
  • Cash bid: the house goes as it stands, handy with a tenant, an inherited property or repairs put off.

Get a lender payoff figure and the county tax statement for your parcel in hand before any conversation.

Two county offices are involved. Valuations come from the Grayson County Appraisal District (205 N Travis Street, 903-893-9673). The Grayson County Tax Assessor-Collector (100 W Houston, 903-892-8297) sends and collects the bills.

The appraisal district's online database lists an estimated tax for each parcel, so it is the fastest way to see what a buyer would carry, and to look at values on nearby streets. Remember that an appraisal is a tax value and an offer can land on either side of it.

A typical Sherman home is taxed by four units. Each unit's rate for 2025, stated per $100 of assessed value, is below, and the city council adopted the city's rate on September 2, 2025.

Rates change from year to year, so ask the Grayson County tax office what your latest bill carries before you quote a figure to a buyer.

Semiconductor work is the big local story. The city's home page features a 300mm wafer fab that has begun production and a $650 million indium phosphide fab expansion at a local optics plant. Those projects bring workers who need housing, and some want a simple, quick purchase near the plants. Strong interest does not erase the need for sensible pricing. Compare any offer against what similar Sherman houses actually closed for, and rely on sold-home records instead of headlines when you set an asking price.

The four rates in the table are separate lines on a Sherman bill: city, school district, county and community college. Sherman ISD carries the largest share of the total, so a school exemption moves your bill more than any other. If you own and live in the house, check with the appraisal district that your homestead exemption is on file ahead of listing. A buyer's agent will usually pull the same parcel page you did, and a missing exemption raises a question you could have answered first.

Sherman has housing from many decades, and an inspector hired by a buyer will study the roof, foundation and wiring of anything old. If you can show records of updates, you start ahead. Gather permits, invoices and warranties before you list.

sections.h2: How Texas bills and penalizes property tax
sections.html:
Expect your bill near October 1 and a due date of January 31. A balance still open on February 1 turns delinquent, with a six percent charge and one percent interest added.

  • The lien and the valuation both date from January 1.
  • You may split the payment: half by November 30, the rest by June 30 of the next year.
  • Owners over 65 or disabled can pay in installments and may get a school tax ceiling.
  • A principal residence earns a $140,000 school homestead exemption, and those older owners get $60,000 more.

At closing the settlement statement splits this year's bill using the closing date. Any earlier balance is paid out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Cash buyers in Sherman can move quickly, so have your folder ready before the first offer arrives. Ask your lender for a payoff figure and print the county tax statement. Look up your parcel in the appraisal district database to see the estimated tax and the value on file. If the house is rented, add the leases, and include any city notices that remain open. Keep them together so a buyer can make a firm offer rather than a guess.

  • Lender payoff figure and the latest tax statement.
  • Records of roof, foundation and wiring updates.
  • Leases and tenant contact details, if any.
  • Any open city notices.

Offers in Sherman differ in more than price. Request proof of funds from each buyer, plus a closing date on paper. Find out who orders the title search and who pays for title and recording. Clarify whether the bid assumes the house stays as is, and how a lien or an old tax balance found in the title search would be handled. If you have a tenant, ask whether the buyer will keep the lease or expects an empty house. When an investor knows your timeline, the choice often comes down to certainty over a slightly higher number.

Keep two addresses handy. For questions about the value on your parcel, the appraisal district is at 205 N Travis Street, phone 903-893-9673. For the bill itself, including what you owe and how to pay, the tax assessor-collector sits at 100 W Houston, phone 903-892-8297. Send an inquiry about a blighted structure to Neighborhood Services at the city. When a title company asks for a tax certificate or payoff, it will contact the second office, so a call from you ahead of time speeds things along.

Grayson County values and sold prices tell different stories. The appraisal district gives you a tax figure, and the district's database lets you compare nearby streets. What buyers pay depends on condition, timing and who is across the table. For a house that needs a roof or foundation work, a cash investor will subtract the cost and risk from the bid. For a house with updates and records, an agent listing may reach buyers who value the work. Both routes work. Pick the one that suits your timeline and the effort you can give it.

Even a rundown house can sell, though you should call the city first. The Quality Neighborhoods Program in Sherman goes after blight and decay, taking down substandard structures with the owner's consent or under a court order.

Open city notices against the house should be cleared or disclosed before you list, since a lender may refuse a loan on a structure with violations. A cash buyer might accept the condition, with the bid reflecting repair or demolition costs. Questions about a particular property go to Neighborhood Services.

Grayson County's clerk keeps the record of every Sherman deed. Your signature must first be acknowledged in front of a notary or another officer with that authority.

Fees follow a statewide schedule with a flat charge for page one, a smaller one for later pages and some records charges. The title company will quote the total.

Unless the lease or the law lets you end it, a lease keeps running, so a buyer may purchase with the tenant in place. Texas removal of a tenant opens with a written notice to vacate. Three days is the norm when the lease is silent. After that, the matter goes to justice court.

  • Service on the tenant must happen no later than four days before trial.
  • County court appeals have to be filed inside five days after judgment.
  • A writ of possession is available once six days have run from final judgment.

An investor can build those timelines into the plan. A buyer who intends to live in the house will usually expect the keys at closing.

Heirs have up to four years after a death to offer a Texas will for probate. If the estate owes nothing besides liens, a muniment of title may let them prove ownership without a full administration. Smaller estates, up to $75,000 excluding the homestead and exempt property, can use a small estate affidavit.

Auctions are held on a month's first Tuesday, following at least 21 days' notice. Within 20 days of the default notice, the borrower may reinstate by paying what is behind. A sale before auction day can keep your equity intact.

faqs.a: Grayson County, where Sherman is the seat. Valuation is the appraisal district's job, and the tax assessor-collector mails the bills.

faqs.q: What city tax rate did Sherman adopt in 2025?
faqs.a: The city lists $0.508000 per $100 of assessed value, adopted September 2, 2025. For your current bill, check with the Grayson County tax office.

faqs.q: Do unpaid taxes stop a sale?
faqs.a: No, though the lien stays with the house. The balance plus penalties and interest gets paid at or before closing, and you will see the amount on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Could the city's blight program touch my house?
faqs.a: It can, if the structure is substandard. Removal happens by consent or court order, and Neighborhood Services can answer questions about a particular address.

faqs.q: How fast can a Sherman house close?
faqs.a: A cash deal skips loan underwriting, so it can finish sooner than a financed one. Title work, probate or lien payoffs can still set the schedule, so ask for proof of funds and a firm date on paper.
